comparison.objective: Open a folding-table leg, slide a brace ring over its knee, and prove the lock under side load; candidate tunes a damper collar, secures it with a setscrew, and proves stopping behavior through repeated impacts.
comparison.physical_skill: Table task uses large-link articulation and linear sleeve/ring sliding over an aligned brace joint. Candidate uses recessed hex-key insertion/re-engagement, captive setscrew loosening, fine rotary collar control, counterholding, and bounded relocking.
comparison.success_condition: Table success requires the leg within 1° of upright, ring at least 12 mm past the knee, hands clear, and survival of a 6 N/1.5 s load with under 3° folding. Candidate requires two ≥0.85 J stops within 0.3–3.30 m/s, ≤12 mm stroke, no hard-stop contact/overload/excessive rebound, plus post-lock setting retention. Candidate rebound, witness-torque, and drift limits are not numeric.
comparison.reason: This is the closest conceptual record because both set a mechanical lock and verify it under load. However, the table tests deployment and linear brace latching, while the candidate tests fine parameter tuning and dynamic energy absorption across repeated cycles; those are meaningfully different abilities.
